newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Leumi offer to contain shares, warrants.
newsitem.headline: Leumi offer to contain shares, warrants.

text.p: The offering in Israel's Bank Leumi will be sold in units containing two ordinary shares and two warrants priced together at a minimum of 10 shekels each, the underwriters said in an announcement on Wednesday.

The offering, which will take place May 27, is valued at $150 million and follows a successful institutional tranche that closed on Monday, which yielded commitments to take 80 percent of the offering.

The size of the offering was boosted by $25 million, equal to 14 percent of the bank's equity (fully diluted), in response to the strong demand from the institutions. Some 20 European institutional investors pre-commmitted to purchasing $120 million worth of shares and warrants.

Each of the warrants entitles holders to one ordinary share. The series three warrant comes due on December 10, 1997 at a conversion price of 5.15 shekels and the series four on August 10, 1998 at a price of 5.51 shekels. The conversion prices are linked to the dollar exchange rate.
Leumi closed at 5.31 shekels on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange on Wednesday.
The lead underwriters are the Israeli brokerages Analyst, IBI and Leader.
Leumi will mark the second major share offering of government-owned bank shares this year, after a successful $196 million secondary offering in April of Israel Discount Bank.
The Israeli government now controls 82 percent of Leumi, Israel's second largest bank, with the remainder traded in the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.
